title: Reproducing Vitkavage, Irene and Massoud 1990: interface charges on four orientations of silicon

sample.paper: “p-type (100), (110), (111), and (511) silicon wafers with resistivities in the 2-20 Ω-cm range” (cleanroom set)
sample.ours: FAMILY: Si_Planar; ORIENTATION: Si100 | Si110 | Si111 | Si511

sample.paper: cleanroom: p-type, 2–20 Ω·cm, dopant not named; non-cleanroom: “Lightly boron-doped p-type … 2-5 Ω-cm”
sample.ours: DOPING: p_type (recorded; no program reads it)
sample.note: The language has no doping field that a program reads. Resistivity is not carried.

sample.paper: A non-cleanroom set made at the University of North Carolina and a cleanroom set oxidized at Duke and metallized at MCNC
sample.ours: one sample family; the thickness dataset marks each row cleanroom or non-cleanroom, the electrical datasets are cleanroom only
sample.note: Two of our six thicknesses (25 nm and 90 nm) are from the non-cleanroom set, whose clean, doping and oxidation times differ from the wafers the electrical values come from.

sample.paper: (100), (111), (511): 4-inch; (110): 3-inch, metallized in a separate run. Guard-ring capacitors, backside contact
sample.note: The (110) wafers went through a different metallization run from the other three orientations.

sample.paper: RCA then, for the non-cleanroom set, a 10 s concentrated HF dip: no deliberate starting oxide
sample.ours: the growth program starts the oxide at the 1965 law's intercept, not at zero

sample.paper: “1 to 5 × 10^11 cm-2” non-cleanroom against about 1.5 × 10^10 cm-2 cleanroom
sample.ours: not in our sample or programs

history.paper: “All wafers were cleaned using the modified RCA cleaning sequences prior to oxidation.”
history.ours: CLEAN: RCA on the sample; no operator reads it
history.note: The HF dip that ends the clean is stated for the non-cleanroom set only; our vocabulary's RCA does not say HF-last.

history.item: Load into the furnace in nitrogen
history.paper: “The wafers were loaded into a double-walled fused-silica tube of the oxidation furnace in an inert N2 ambient”
history.note: No duration, temperature or push rate is stated, so it cannot be written as a RUN.

history.paper: Table I gives temperature and time; the gas is only “the oxidizing ambient” under “similar processing conditions”
history.ours: RUN Oxidation DURATION 3600 TEMP 1000->1000 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: Dry O2 with under 6 ppm water is stated for the non-cleanroom set; for the cleanroom set we assume the same.

history.item: Fast pull into the endcap, in oxygen
history.paper: “pulled fast into the endcap in the oxidizing ambient with a pull time shorter than 5 sec”
history.ours: RUN Pull DURATION 5 TEMP 1000->400 AMBIENT dry_O2
history.note: The pull time is the paper's. The temperature the wafer reaches is not stated; 400 °C is our assumption. The datasets' recipe for this wafer has no pull step.

history.item: Stored in a nitrogen dry box
history.paper: “Upon cooling, the wafers were stored in a dry box continuously purged with pure nitrogen until all oxidations were completed.”
“A blanket layer of aluminum was evaporated … using a resistively heated evaporator”; guard-ring capacitors by lithography; backside oxide etched
history.note: Recorded on the source in the library (metal: resistively heated aluminium); no program reads it.

history.paper: “a 30 min post-metallization anneal (PMA) at 400°C in forming gas (FG), consisting of 10% H2 and 90% N2”
history.ours: RUN PostMetalAnneal DURATION 1800 TEMP 400->400 AMBIENT forming_gas_H2

history.paper: 1 MHz and quasi-static C-V, ramp under 100 mV/s; Qf from the flatband voltage
history.note: The work-function difference used for Qf is not stated.

history.item: Post-oxidation anneal in nitrogen, some wafers
history.paper: “Some wafers received a post-oxidation anneal (POA) in N2 at the oxidation temperature.” Duration and which wafers are not stated
history.note: If any tabulated wafer had this anneal, its fixed charge would be lower than a fast-pull wafer's. The report does not say which.

steps.name: Clean
steps.label: Pre-oxidation clean
steps.paper: “All wafers were cleaned using the modified RCA cleaning sequences prior to oxidation.”
steps.timing: Only the HF dip (10 s) is timed, and only for the non-cleanroom set

steps.name: Load
steps.label: Load into the furnace in nitrogen
steps.paper: “The wafers were loaded into a double-walled fused-silica tube of the oxidation furnace in an inert N2 ambient”
steps.timing: No push rate, no time in nitrogen before oxygen, no ramp

steps.name: Oxidation
steps.label: Dry oxidation, 1000 °C, 1 h
steps.isl: RUN Oxidation DURATION 3600 TEMP 1000->1000 AMBIENT dry_O2
steps.paper: Table I gives temperature and time; the gas is only “the oxidizing ambient” under “similar processing conditions”
steps.timing: Table I. Whether the time counts from loading or from the gas switch is not said

steps.name: Pull
steps.label: Fast pull into the endcap, in oxygen
steps.isl: RUN Pull DURATION 5 TEMP 1000->400 AMBIENT dry_O2
steps.paper: “pulled fast into the endcap in the oxidizing ambient with a pull time shorter than 5 sec”
steps.timing: “shorter than 5 sec” is an upper bound; how long the wafer then cools in the endcap is not given

steps.name: Store
steps.label: Stored in a nitrogen dry box
steps.paper: “Upon cooling, the wafers were stored in a dry box continuously purged with pure nitrogen until all oxidations were completed.”
steps.timing: “until all oxidations were completed”: days, not given

steps.name: Metal
steps.label: Aluminium evaporated
steps.paper: “A blanket layer of aluminum was evaporated … using a resistively heated evaporator”; guard-ring capacitors by lithography; backside oxide etched

steps.paper: “a 30 min post-metallization anneal (PMA) at 400°C in forming gas (FG), consisting of 10% H2 and 90% N2”
steps.timing: 30 min at temperature; ramp up and cool down not given
